standard_prerequisites.name: Descent of the property of being a closed immersion along an fpqc covering
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion (canonical Stacks tag 02L6); invoked at proof line 247
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that X -> X' is a closed immersion once its base changes are; the surjectivity step and the assembly into a thickening are retained in the counted span.

core_obligations: Unwind the statement: the assertion means that for a morphism of schemes X -> X' and an fpqc covering {g_i : X'_i -> X'} such that every base change X_i -> X'_i is a thickening, the original X -> X' is a thickening (proof lines 241-244).
Get surjectivity: since the morphisms g_i are jointly surjective, the morphism X -> X' is surjective, because the X_i cover X' and each X_i lies over X (proof lines 245-246).

Conclude that it is a thickening: descent of the property of being a closed immersion along the fpqc covering makes X -> X' a closed immersion, and a surjective closed immersion is a thickening; the author then states that the case of first order thickenings is left unproved (proof lines 246-250).
proof_roadmap: Translate fpqc locality into the concrete descent statement for a covering of the target (proof lines 241-244).
Use joint surjectivity of the covering to obtain surjectivity of X -> X' (proof lines 245-246).
Apply descent of closed immersions and conclude, leaving the first order case to the reader (proof lines 246-250).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the property of being a thickening, and likewise of being a first order thickening, descends along an fpqc covering of the target (statement lines 236-237). The proof reduces the locality to two standard ingredients that have to be combined in the right order: joint surjectivity of the covering gives surjectivity of X -> X', and descent of the closed-immersion property along the covering gives that X -> X' is a closed immersion, after which a surjective closed immersion is by definition a thickening (proof lines 245-248). The author explicitly leaves the first order case unproved, saying it is analogous; that is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: short, with one genuine reduction step, and no construction of its own.
